propositions: MCP tool failures currently lack the structured error discriminator (error_code) that the CLI already emits via error_envelope, forcing agents to pattern-match human prose instead of machine codes

The CLI emits distinct error codes from scattered sites (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, show_failed, deps_failed) but no single shared vocabulary or classifier exists, and no library-side error_code_for function is exported
MCP surfaces failures as unstructured exception prose or two divergent ad-hoc partial shapes (explain_criterion and llm responses) with no uniform error code, breaking agent error branching logic

The solution adds error_code_for(exc)->str classifier + KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset in _errors.py re-exported to the library, classifies by exception type (not message substring) to satisfy AC4, and raises McpEnvelopeError on the MCP boundary carrying structured .envelope dict

MCP guard migrates exception-raised AND return-shaped soft errors to emit vocabulary codes (criterion_unknown_id, llm_unavailable, etc.) while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable), ensuring no code exists on one interface only and CLI output remains byte-identical
